data.text: Kai has had a three-day headache, worse at the temples on both sides, after cutting back sharply on coffee last week.
Amara advised Kai to hydrate, take a steady small caffeine dose, taper by a quarter every few days, and use a simple painkiller if needed.
Amara told Kai red flags needing same-day emergency care: thunderclap headache, fever with neck stiffness, one-sided weakness, confusion, vision changes, or headache waking him at night.
Amara argued for a nationwide four-day week: a protected-rest health and safety intervention, citing burnout cuts, better sleep, and stable patient care in pilots.
Mei's strongest opposing point: holding coverage constant took 18–27% more staffed hours, hitting small shift-based employers hardest.
Debate verdict: the Against side made the stronger case, as neither side closed whether staffed hours rise or turnover savings repay costs.
